title: The Past Indicative of Strong Verbs
subtitle: Ic rād, wē ridon — ablaut in action.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of The Past Indicative of Strong Verbs.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: The past tense of strong verbs uses a different root vowel from the present. Class I verbs (rīdan): present ī, past singular ā, past plural i. Ic rād, þū ride, hē rād, wē/gē/hīe ridon. The second principal part is the past singular, the third is the past plural.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Ic rād (I rode), þū ride (you rode), hē rād (he rode), wē ridon (we rode).
